steps.message:
The fix is complete and the project builds successfully.

## Root cause

The app was writing settings to one `SharedPreferences` file and reading them from a **different** one.

- Everything in the app reads settings via `Util.getPreferences()` → `context.getSharedPreferences("org.moire.ultrasonic_preferences", 0)` (`Constants.PREFERENCES_FILE_NAME`).
- But `ServerSettingsFragment` (and `SettingsFragment`) used `PreferenceManager.getDefaultSharedPreferences()`, which resolves to `"<applicationId>_preferences"`. `ultrasonic/build.gradle` sets `applicationIdSuffix ".debug"`, so on a debug build that is **`"org.moire.ultrasonic.debug_preferences"`** — a completely separate file. The `PreferenceFragment` itself also persisted its preference widgets there, since `addPreferencesFromResource()` uses the fragment's own `PreferenceManager`.

So the server URL/username/password the user typed landed in `org.moire.ultrasonic.debug_preferences`, while `MusicServiceFactory.createSubsonicApiClient()` looked in `org.moire.ultrasonic_preferences`, found `serverUrl == null`, and hit this fallback:

```java
Log.i("MusicServiceFactory", "Server credentials is not available");
return new SubsonicAPIClient("http://localhost", "", "", ...);
```

That is exactly the reported `Failed to connect to localhost/127.0.0.1:80`. Two details in the report confirm it: the logcat process is `org.moire.ultrasonic.debug` (a debug build, where the two names diverge), and "works fine with 2.2.2" — in a *release* build the default name coincidentally equals `PREFERENCES_FILE_NAME`, so the bug is invisible there.

## Changes

1. **`ServerSettingsFragment.java`** — point the fragment's `PreferenceManager` at `Constants.PREFERENCES_FILE_NAME` *before* `addPreferencesFromResource()`, and read via `Util.getPreferences()`.
2. **`SettingsFragment.java`** — same fix; it had the identical defect for all the main app settings.
3. **`Util.getActiveServers()`** — was the one remaining reader using default prefs, so the server count was read from the wrong file too; switched to `getPreferences(context)`.
4. **`ServerSettingsFragment`** — added `invalidateCachedMusicService()`, called when the active server's URL/username/password/SSL/LDAP settings change. `MusicServiceFactory` caches the `SubsonicAPIClient` in a static, so without this an edit to the active server would still be served by a stale client until something else called `Util.setActiveServer()`.

I verified no `getDefaultSharedPreferences` call sites remain in `ultrasonic/src/`, and `./gradlew clean assembleDebug` reports `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`.

One note worth flagging: this fix changes which file settings are stored in, so on a debug build any server already configured under the old `*.debug_preferences` file will appear reset and need re-entering. Release builds are unaffected, since their default name already matched. If you'd prefer, I can add a one-time migration that copies entries from the default file into `PREFERENCES_FILE_NAME` on first launch.

In this Android project (Ultrasonic music player), find the code related to SubsonicAPIClient construction, SubsonicClientConfiguration, MusicServiceFactory, RESTMusicService, and how server URL/username/password settings are read (e.g. Util.getRestUrl, shared preferences keys like Constants.PREFERENCES_KEY_SERVER_URL). Also find ServerSettingsFragment. Report the absolute file paths and the key relevant code snippets (with line numbers) showing how the API client is created and configured with the server URL. Be thorough.

118	     * It detects the response `Content-Type` and tries to parse subsonic error if there is one.
119	     *
120	     * Prefer this method over [SubsonicAPIDefinition.stream] as this handles error cases.
121	     */
122	    fun stream(id: String, maxBitrate: Int? = null, offset: Long? = null): StreamResponse =
123	            handleStreamResponse {
124	                api.stream(id, maxBitrate, offset = offset).execute()
125	            }
126	
127	    /**
128	     * Convenient method to get user avatar using [username].
129	     *
130	     * It detects the response `Content-Type` and tries to parse subsonic error if there is one.
131	     *
132	     * Prefer this method over [SubsonicAPIDefinition.getAvatar] as this handles error cases.
133	     */
134	    fun getAvatar(username: String): StreamResponse = handleStreamResponse {
135	        api.getAvatar(username).execute()
136	    }

138	    private inline fun handleStreamResponse(apiCall: () -> Response<ResponseBody>): StreamResponse {
139	        val response = apiCall()
140	        return if (response.isSuccessful) {
141	            val responseBody = response.body()
142	            val contentType = responseBody.contentType()
143	            if (contentType != null &&
144	                    contentType.type().equals("application", true) &&
145	                    contentType.subtype().equals("json", true)) {
146	                val error = jacksonMapper.readValue<SubsonicResponse>(responseBody.byteStream())
147	                StreamResponse(apiError = error.error, responseHttpCode = response.code())
148	            } else {
149	                StreamResponse(stream = responseBody.byteStream(),
150	                        responseHttpCode = response.code())
151	            }
152	        } else {
153	            StreamResponse(responseHttpCode = response.code())
154	        }
155	    }
156	
157	    /**
158	     * Get stream url.
159	     *
160	     * Calling this method do actual connection to the backend, though not downloading all content.
161	     *
162	     * Consider do not use this method, but [stream] call.
163	     */
164	    fun getStreamUrl(id: String): String {
165	        val request = api.stream(id).execute()
166	        val url = request.raw().request().url().toString()
167	        if (request.isSuccessful) {
168	            request.body().close()
169	        }
170	        return url
171	    }

174	        val loggingInterceptor = HttpLoggingInterceptor()
175	        loggingInterceptor.level = HttpLoggingInterceptor.Level.BODY

183	            override fun checkServerTrusted(p0: Array<out X509Certificate>?, p1: String?) {}
184	            override fun getAcceptedIssuers(): Array<X509Certificate> = emptyArray()

4	import com.fasterxml.jackson.core.JsonParseException
5	import com.fasterxml.jackson.core.JsonToken
6	import okhttp3.Interceptor
7	import okhttp3.Interceptor.Chain
8	import okhttp3.Response
9	import org.moire.ultrasonic.api.subsonic.SubsonicAPIVersions
10	import java.io.IOException
11	
12	private const val DEFAULT_PEEK_BYTE_COUNT = 1000L
13	
14	/**
15	 * Special [Interceptor] that adds client supported version to request and tries to update it
16	 * from server response.
17	 *
18	 * Optionally [notifier] will be invoked on version change.
19	 *
20	 * @author Yahor Berdnikau
21	 */
22	internal class VersionInterceptor(
23	        internal var protocolVersion: SubsonicAPIVersions,
24	        private val notifier: (SubsonicAPIVersions) -> Unit = {}) : Interceptor {
25	    private val jsonFactory = JsonFactory()
26	
27	    override fun intercept(chain: Chain): okhttp3.Response {
28	        val originalRequest = chain.request()
29	
30	        val newRequest = originalRequest.newBuilder()
31	                .url(originalRequest
32	                        .url()
33	                        .newBuilder()
34	                        .addQueryParameter("v", protocolVersion.restApiVersion)
35	                        .build())
36	                .build()
37	
38	        val response = chain.proceed(newRequest)
39	        if (response.isSuccessful) {
40	            val isJson = response.body()?.contentType()?.subtype()?.equals("json", true) ?: false
41	            if (isJson) {
42	                tryUpdateProtocolVersion(response)
43	            }
44	        }
45	
46	        return response
47	    }
48	
49	    private fun tryUpdateProtocolVersion(response: Response) {
50	        val content = response.peekBody(DEFAULT_PEEK_BYTE_COUNT)
51	                .byteStream().bufferedReader().readText()
52	
53	        try {
54	            val jsonReader = jsonFactory.createParser(content)
55	            jsonReader.nextToken()
56	            if (jsonReader.currentToken == JsonToken.START_OBJECT) {
57	                while (jsonReader.currentName != "version" &&
58	                        jsonReader.currentToken != null) {
59	                    jsonReader.nextToken()
60	                }
61	                val versionStr = jsonReader.nextTextValue()
62	                if (versionStr != null) {
63	                    try {
64	                        protocolVersion = SubsonicAPIVersions.fromApiVersion(versionStr)
65	                        notifier(protocolVersion)
66	                    } catch (e: IllegalArgumentException) {
67	                        // no-op
68	                    }
69	                }
70	            }
71	        } catch (io: IOException) {
72	            // no-op
73	        } catch (parse: JsonParseException) {
74	            // no-op
75	        }
76	    }
77	}

extra.final_message:
The fix is complete and the project builds successfully.

## Root cause

The app was writing settings to one `SharedPreferences` file and reading them from a **different** one.

- Everything in the app reads settings via `Util.getPreferences()` → `context.getSharedPreferences("org.moire.ultrasonic_preferences", 0)` (`Constants.PREFERENCES_FILE_NAME`).
- But `ServerSettingsFragment` (and `SettingsFragment`) used `PreferenceManager.getDefaultSharedPreferences()`, which resolves to `"<applicationId>_preferences"`. `ultrasonic/build.gradle` sets `applicationIdSuffix ".debug"`, so on a debug build that is **`"org.moire.ultrasonic.debug_preferences"`** — a completely separate file. The `PreferenceFragment` itself also persisted its preference widgets there, since `addPreferencesFromResource()` uses the fragment's own `PreferenceManager`.

So the server URL/username/password the user typed landed in `org.moire.ultrasonic.debug_preferences`, while `MusicServiceFactory.createSubsonicApiClient()` looked in `org.moire.ultrasonic_preferences`, found `serverUrl == null`, and hit this fallback:

```java
Log.i("MusicServiceFactory", "Server credentials is not available");
return new SubsonicAPIClient("http://localhost", "", "", ...);
```

That is exactly the reported `Failed to connect to localhost/127.0.0.1:80`. Two details in the report confirm it: the logcat process is `org.moire.ultrasonic.debug` (a debug build, where the two names diverge), and "works fine with 2.2.2" — in a *release* build the default name coincidentally equals `PREFERENCES_FILE_NAME`, so the bug is invisible there.

## Changes

1. **`ServerSettingsFragment.java`** — point the fragment's `PreferenceManager` at `Constants.PREFERENCES_FILE_NAME` *before* `addPreferencesFromResource()`, and read via `Util.getPreferences()`.
2. **`SettingsFragment.java`** — same fix; it had the identical defect for all the main app settings.
3. **`Util.getActiveServers()`** — was the one remaining reader using default prefs, so the server count was read from the wrong file too; switched to `getPreferences(context)`.
4. **`ServerSettingsFragment`** — added `invalidateCachedMusicService()`, called when the active server's URL/username/password/SSL/LDAP settings change. `MusicServiceFactory` caches the `SubsonicAPIClient` in a static, so without this an edit to the active server would still be served by a stale client until something else called `Util.setActiveServer()`.

I verified no `getDefaultSharedPreferences` call sites remain in `ultrasonic/src/`, and `./gradlew clean assembleDebug` reports `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`.

One note worth flagging: this fix changes which file settings are stored in, so on a debug build any server already configured under the old `*.debug_preferences` file will appear reset and need re-entering. Release builds are unaffected, since their default name already matched. If you'd prefer, I can add a one-time migration that copies entries from the default file into `PREFERENCES_FILE_NAME` on first launch.
